10	# Separatedness brick 3: pullback along the projection is injective on Picard groups
11	
12	For `C` proper, geometrically irreducible and geometrically reduced over a field `k` and
13	**any** test object `T` over `Spec k`, pullback of Čech Picard classes along the second
14	projection `pr : (C ⊗ T).left ⟶ T.left` is injective
15	(`AlgebraicGeometry.Over.prPullback_injective`) — brick 3 of the separatedness ledger
16	(design §4.4), the cocycle recast of "a line bundle pulled back from the base which
17	trivializes on the product was trivial", the projection step of Kleiman,
18	*The Picard Scheme*, Theorem 2.5(1).
19	
20	## The section-level engine
21	
22	Everything reduces to the section rings: for an **affine** open `V ⊆ T.left`, pullback of
23	sections along the projection is bijective,
24	`Γ(T.left, V) ≅ Γ((C ⊗ T).left, pr⁻¹ V)` (`Over.isIso_appLE_snd`). This is brick 2
25	(`Over.isIso_appTop_snd_overSpec`, `Picard/UniversalSections.lean`) freed from its
26	`T = Spec A`, `V = ⊤` special case: the qcqs pushout square of
27	`Mathlib.AlgebraicGeometry.Morphisms.Flat` is applied to the pullback square
28	`(C ⊗ T).left = C.left ×_{Spec k} T.left` with the *affine* slot at `V ⊆ T.left` and the
29	*qcqs* slot at `⊤ ⊆ C.left`, and the `k ≅ Γ(C.left, 𝒪)` leg (Wave 1) transfers the
30	isomorphism across the square. Flatness of `T.hom` is automatic over a field
31	(`AlgebraicGeometry.Flat.of_field`). By sheaf separation the injectivity half extends to
32	**arbitrary** opens `W ⊆ T.left` (`Over.appLE_snd_injective`), which is why no affineness
33	or quasi-separatedness hypothesis on `T` survives into the final statement.
34	
35	## The cocycle assembly
36	
37	A Picard class on `T` dying on `C ⊗ T` is represented, after refining to an affine
38	pointed cover `𝒰` (`Scheme.PointedCover.exists_isAffineOpen_le`), by a unit cocycle `γ`

44	injectivity of pullback on `𝒰 t ⊓ 𝒰 t'`.
45	-/

6	import AlgebraicJacobian.Descent.UnitDescent
7	
8	/-!
9	# Base change of descent 1-cocycles along maps of algebras
10	
11	Continuation of `AlgebraicJacobian.Descent.UnitDescent`: the base change of a descent
12	1-cocycle along a map `h : B →ₐ[A] B'` of `A`-algebras is a descent 1-cocycle
13	(`Module.IsDescentCocycle.map`), and for faithfully flat `B, B'` the descended module —
14	hence the Picard class — does not change (`Module.descendedMapEquiv`,
15	`Module.IsDescentCocycle.picClass_map`).
16	-/
17	
18	universe u
19	
20	open TensorProduct
21	
22	namespace Module
23	
24	variable {A B : Type u} [CommRing A] [CommRing B] [Algebra A B]
25	variable {u : (B ⊗[A] B)ˣ}
26	
27	/-! ## Base change of cocycles along maps of algebras -/
28	
29	section map
30	
31	variable {B' : Type u} [CommRing B'] [Algebra A B'] (h : B →ₐ[A] B')
32	
33	/-- The base change of a descent cocycle along a map of `A`-algebras is a descent
34	cocycle. -/
35	theorem IsDescentCocycle.map {u : (B ⊗[A] B)ˣ} (hu : IsDescentCocycle u) :
36	    IsDescentCocycle (Units.map (Algebra.TensorProduct.map h h).toRingHom.toMonoidHom u) := by
37	  -- Naturality: `lmul' ∘ (map h h) = h ∘ lmul'` and
38	  -- `descentFaceᵢⱼ ∘ (map h h) = (map h (map h h)) ∘ descentFaceᵢⱼ` (check on pure
39	  -- tensors by `Algebra.TensorProduct.ext` or by `TensorProduct.induction_on`); apply `h`
40	  -- to the two conditions of `hu`.
41	  have hlmul : ∀ w : B ⊗[A] B,
42	      Algebra.TensorProduct.lmul' A (S := B') (Algebra.TensorProduct.map h h w)
43	        = h (Algebra.TensorProduct.lmul' A (S := B) w) := by
44	    intro w
45	    induction w with
46	    | zero => simp
47	    | tmul x y => simp [Algebra.TensorProduct.lmul'_apply_tmul]
48	    | add x y hx hy => simp only [map_add, hx, hy]
49	  have hface₁₂ : ∀ w : B ⊗[A] B,
50	      descentFace₁₂ A B' (Algebra.TensorProduct.map h h w)
51	        = Algebra.TensorProduct.map h (Algebra.TensorProduct.map h h)
52	            (descentFace₁₂ A B w) := by
53	    intro w
54	    induction w with
55	    | zero => simp
56	    | tmul x y => simp
57	    | add x y hx hy => simp only [map_add, hx, hy]
58	  have hface₁₃ : ∀ w : B ⊗[A] B,
59	      descentFace₁₃ A B' (Algebra.TensorProduct.map h h w)
60	        = Algebra.TensorProduct.map h (Algebra.TensorProduct.map h h)
61	            (descentFace₁₃ A B w) := by
62	    intro w
63	    induction w with
64	    | zero => simp
65	    | tmul x y => simp
66	    | add x y hx hy => simp only [map_add, hx, hy]
67	  have hface₂₃ : ∀ w : B ⊗[A] B,
68	      descentFace₂₃ A B' (Algebra.TensorProduct.map h h w)
69	        = Algebra.TensorProduct.map h (Algebra.TensorProduct.map h h)
70	            (descentFace₂₃ A B w) := by
71	    intro w
72	    simp
73	  constructor
74	  · change Algebra.TensorProduct.lmul' A (S := B') (Algebra.TensorProduct.map h h u.val) = 1
75	    rw [hlmul, hu.lmul'_eq_one, map_one]
76	  · change descentFace₂₃ A B' (Algebra.TensorProduct.map h h u.val)
77	        * descentFace₁₂ A B' (Algebra.TensorProduct.map h h u.val)
78	      = descentFace₁₃ A B' (Algebra.TensorProduct.map h h u.val)
79	    rw [hface₂₃, hface₁₂, hface₁₃, ← map_mul, hu.cocycle]
80	
81	/-- Base change of the descended module along a map of faithfully flat `A`-algebras:
82	the descended module does not change. -/
83	noncomputable def descendedMapEquiv [Module.FaithfullyFlat A B] [Module.FaithfullyFlat A B']
84	    {u : (B ⊗[A] B)ˣ} (hu : IsDescentCocycle u) :
85	    hu.descended ≃ₗ[A] (hu.map h).descended := by
86	  -- Route: `equivDescended (DescentDatum.ofUnit _ (hu.map h)) e' he'` where
87	  -- `e' : B' ⊗[A] descended u ≃ₗ[B'] B'` is `liftBaseChange` of `h ∘ subtype`, bijective
88	  -- because it factors as
89	  -- `B' ⊗[A] M ≃ B' ⊗[B] (B ⊗[A] M) ≃ B' ⊗[B] B ≃ B'`
90	  -- (`AlgebraTensorModule.cancelBaseChange` and the descent equivalence of `u`), and the
91	  -- compatibility `he'` reduces on pure tensors to applying `map h h` to
92	  -- `u * (m ⊗ₜ 1) = 1 ⊗ₜ m`.
93	  have hbij : Function.Bijective
94	      ⇑((h.toLinearMap ∘ₗ hu.descended.subtype).liftBaseChange B') := by
95	    letI : Algebra B B' := h.toRingHom.toAlgebra
96	    haveI : IsScalarTower A B B' := IsScalarTower.of_algebraMap_eq fun a => (h.commutes a).symm
97	    have hpt : ∀ x : B' ⊗[A] hu.descended,
98	        ((h.toLinearMap ∘ₗ hu.descended.subtype).liftBaseChange B') x
99	          = (((AlgebraTensorModule.cancelBaseChange A B B' B' hu.descended).symm.trans
100	              (LinearEquiv.baseChange B B' (B ⊗[A] hu.descended) B
101	                (DescentDatum.ofUnit u hu).descentEquiv)).trans
102	              (AlgebraTensorModule.rid B B' B')) x := by
103	      intro x
104	      induction x with
105	      | zero => simp
106	      | tmul b' m =>
107	          change b' * h (m : B) = ((1 : B) • ((m : B))) • b'
108	          rw [one_smul, Algebra.smul_def, RingHom.algebraMap_toAlgebra]
109	          exact mul_comm _ _
110	      | add x y hx hy => simp only [map_add, hx, hy]
111	    rw [show ⇑((h.toLinearMap ∘ₗ hu.descended.subtype).liftBaseChange B')
112	        = ⇑(((AlgebraTensorModule.cancelBaseChange A B B' B' hu.descended).symm.trans
113	              (LinearEquiv.baseChange B B' (B ⊗[A] hu.descended) B
114	                (DescentDatum.ofUnit u hu).descentEquiv)).trans
115	              (AlgebraTensorModule.rid B B' B'))
116	      from funext hpt]
117	    exact (((AlgebraTensorModule.cancelBaseChange A B B' B' hu.descended).symm.trans
118	      (LinearEquiv.baseChange B B' (B ⊗[A] hu.descended) B
119	        (DescentDatum.ofUnit u hu).descentEquiv)).trans
120	      (AlgebraTensorModule.rid B B' B')).bijective
121	  refine (DescentDatum.ofUnit _ (hu.map h)).equivDescended
122	    (LinearEquiv.ofBijective ((h.toLinearMap ∘ₗ hu.descended.subtype).liftBaseChange B') hbij)
123	    fun x => ?_
124	  induction x with
125	  | zero => simp
126	  | tmul b' m =>
127	      have hm : u.val * ((m : B) ⊗ₜ[A] (1 : B)) = 1 ⊗ₜ (m : B) := hu.mem_descended.mp m.2
128	      have hm' : Algebra.TensorProduct.map h h u.val * (h (m : B) ⊗ₜ[A] (1 : B'))
129	          = 1 ⊗ₜ h (m : B) := by
130	        have := congrArg (Algebra.TensorProduct.map h h) hm
131	        simpa using this
132	      simp only [ofUnit_coaction, unitCoaction_apply, DescentDatum.baseChange_coaction,
133	        LinearMap.baseChange_tmul, LinearMap.coe_restrictScalars, LinearEquiv.coe_coe,
134	        TensorProduct.mk_apply]
135	      change Algebra.TensorProduct.map h h u.val * ((b' * h (m : B)) ⊗ₜ[A] (1 : B'))
136	        = b' ⊗ₜ[A] ((1 : B') * h (m : B))
137	      rw [one_mul,
138	        show (b' * h (m : B)) ⊗ₜ[A] (1 : B')
139	            = (b' ⊗ₜ[A] (1 : B')) * (h (m : B) ⊗ₜ[A] (1 : B')) by
140	          rw [Algebra.TensorProduct.tmul_mul_tmul, mul_one],
141	        show b' ⊗ₜ[A] h (m : B) = (b' ⊗ₜ[A] (1 : B')) * ((1 : B') ⊗ₜ[A] h (m : B)) by
142	          rw [Algebra.TensorProduct.tmul_mul_tmul, mul_one, one_mul]]
143	      linear_combination (b' ⊗ₜ[A] (1 : B')) * hm'
144	  | add x y hx hy => simp only [map_add, hx, hy]
145	
146	@[simp]
147	theorem IsDescentCocycle.picClass_map [Module.FaithfullyFlat A B]
148	    [Module.FaithfullyFlat A B'] {u : (B ⊗[A] B)ˣ} (hu : IsDescentCocycle u) :
149	    (hu.map h).picClass = hu.picClass :=
150	  (CommRing.Pic.mk_eq_mk_iff.mpr ⟨(descendedMapEquiv h hu).symm⟩)
151	
152	end map
153	end Module

1	/-

6	module
7	
8	public import Mathlib.Algebra.Category.ModuleCat.Monoidal.Symmetric
9	public import Mathlib.CategoryTheory.Monoidal.Skeleton
10	public import Mathlib.LinearAlgebra.Contraction
11	public import Mathlib.LinearAlgebra.LinearDisjoint
12	public import Mathlib.RingTheory.Ideal.AssociatedPrime.Finiteness
13	public import Mathlib.RingTheory.LocalRing.Module
14	public import Mathlib.RingTheory.UniqueFactorizationDomain.ClassGroup
15	
16	/-!
17	# The Picard group of a commutative ring
18	
19	This file defines the Picard group `CommRing.Pic R` of a commutative ring `R` as the type of
20	invertible `R`-modules (in the sense that `M` is invertible if there exists another `R`-module
21	`N` such that `M ⊗[R] N ≃ₗ[R] R`) up to isomorphism, equipped with tensor product as multiplication.
22	
23	## Main definition
24	
25	- `Module.Invertible R M` says that the canonical map `Mᵛ ⊗[R] M → R` is an isomorphism.
26	  To show that `M` is invertible, it suffices to provide an arbitrary `R`-module `N`
27	  and an isomorphism `N ⊗[R] M ≃ₗ[R] R`, see `Module.Invertible.right`.
28	
29	- `ClassGroup.equivPic`: the class group of a domain is isomorphic to the Picard group.
30	
31	## Main results
32	
33	- An invertible module is finite and projective (provided as instances).
34	
35	- `Module.Invertible.free_iff_linearEquiv`: an invertible module is free iff it is isomorphic to
36	  the ring, i.e. its class is trivial in the Picard group.
37	
38	- `Submodule.ker_unitsToPic`, `Submodule.range_unitsToPic`: exactness of the sequence
39	  `1 → Rˣ → Aˣ → (Submodule R A)ˣ → Pic R → Pic A` at the last two spots.
40	  See Theorem 2.4 in [RobertsSingh1993] or Exercise I.3.7(iv) and Proposition I.3.5 in [Weibel2013].
41	
42	## References
43	
44	- https://qchu.wordpress.com/2014/10/19/the-picard-groups/
45	- https://mathoverflow.net/questions/13768/what-is-the-right-definition-of-the-picard-group-of-a-commutative-ring
46	- https://mathoverflow.net/questions/375725/picard-group-vs-class-group
47	- [Weibel2013], https://sites.math.rutgers.edu/~weibel/Kbook/Kbook.I.pdf
48	- [Stacks: Picard groups of rings](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/0AFW)
49	
50	## TODO
51	
52	Show:
53	- Invertible modules over a commutative ring have the same cardinality as the ring.
54	
55	- Establish other characterizations of invertible modules, e.g. they are modules that
56	  become free of rank one when localized at every prime ideal.
57	  See [Stacks: Finite projective modules](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/00NX).
58	- Connect to invertible sheaves on `Spec R`. More generally, connect projective `R`-modules of
59	  constant finite rank to locally free sheaves on `Spec R`.
60	- Exhibit isomorphism with sheaf cohomology `H¹(Spec R, 𝓞ˣ)`.
61	-/
62	
63	@[expose] public section
64	
65	open TensorProduct
66	
67	universe u v
68	
69	variable (R : Type u) (M : Type v) (N P Q A : Type*) [CommSemiring R]
70	variable [AddCommMonoid M] [AddCommMonoid N] [AddCommMonoid P] [AddCommMonoid Q]
71	variable [Module R M] [Module R N] [Module R P] [Module R Q]
72	
73	namespace Module
74	
75	/-- An `R`-module `M` is invertible if the canonical map `Mᵛ ⊗[R] M → R` is an isomorphism,
76	where `Mᵛ` is the `R`-dual of `M`. -/
77	protected class Invertible : Prop where
78	  bijective : Function.Bijective (contractLeft R M)
79	
80	namespace Invertible
81	
82	/-- Promote the canonical map `Mᵛ ⊗[R] M → R` to a linear equivalence for invertible `M`. -/
83	noncomputable def linearEquiv [Module.Invertible R M] : Module.Dual R M ⊗[R] M ≃ₗ[R] R :=
84	  .ofBijective _ Invertible.bijective
85	
86	variable {R M N}
87	
88	section LinearEquiv
89	
90	variable (e : M ⊗[R] N ≃ₗ[R] R)
91	
92	/-- The canonical isomorphism between a module and the result of tensoring it
93	from the left by two mutually dual invertible modules. -/
94	noncomputable abbrev leftCancelEquiv : M ⊗[R] (N ⊗[R] P) ≃ₗ[R] P :=
95	  (TensorProduct.assoc R M N P).symm ≪≫ₗ e.rTensor P ≪≫ₗ TensorProduct.lid R P
96	
97	/-- The canonical isomorphism between a module and the result of tensoring it
98	from the right by two mutually dual invertible modules. -/
99	noncomputable abbrev rightCancelEquiv : (P ⊗[R] M) ⊗[R] N ≃ₗ[R] P :=
100	  TensorProduct.assoc R P M N ≪≫ₗ e.lTensor P ≪≫ₗ TensorProduct.rid R P
101	
102	variable {P Q} in
103	theorem leftCancelEquiv_comp_lTensor_comp_symm (f : P →ₗ[R] Q) :
104	    leftCancelEquiv Q e ∘ₗ (f.lTensor N).lTensor M ∘ₗ (leftCancelEquiv P e).symm = f := by
105	  rw [← LinearMap.comp_assoc, LinearEquiv.comp_toLinearMap_symm_eq]; ext; simp
106	
107	variable {P Q} in
108	theorem rightCancelEquiv_comp_rTensor_comp_symm (f : P →ₗ[R] Q) :
109	    rightCancelEquiv Q e ∘ₗ (f.rTensor M).rTensor N ∘ₗ (rightCancelEquiv P e).symm = f := by
110	  rw [← LinearMap.comp_assoc, LinearEquiv.comp_toLinearMap_symm_eq]; ext; simp
111	
112	/-- If M is invertible, `rTensorHom M` admits an inverse. -/
113	noncomputable def rTensorInv : (P ⊗[R] M →ₗ[R] Q ⊗[R] M) →ₗ[R] (P →ₗ[R] Q) :=
114	  ((rightCancelEquiv Q e).congrRight ≪≫ₗ (rightCancelEquiv P e).congrLeft _ R) ∘ₗ
115	    LinearMap.rTensorHom N
116	
117	theorem rTensorInv_leftInverse : Function.LeftInverse (rTensorInv P Q e) (.rTensorHom M) :=
118	  fun _ ↦ by
119	    simp_rw [rTensorInv, LinearEquiv.coe_trans, LinearMap.comp_apply, LinearEquiv.coe_toLinearMap]
120	    rw [← LinearEquiv.eq_symm_apply]
121	    ext; simp [LinearEquiv.congrLeft, LinearEquiv.congrRight, LinearEquiv.arrowCongrAddEquiv]
122	
123	theorem rTensorInv_injective : Function.Injective (rTensorInv P Q e) := by
124	  simpa [rTensorInv] using (rTensorInv_leftInverse _ _ <| TensorProduct.comm R N M ≪≫ₗ e).injective
125	
126	/-- If `M` is an invertible `R`-module, `(· ⊗[R] M)` is an auto-equivalence of the category
127	of `R`-modules. -/
128	@[simps!] noncomputable def rTensorEquiv : (P →ₗ[R] Q) ≃ₗ[R] (P ⊗[R] M →ₗ[R] Q ⊗[R] M) where
129	  __ := LinearMap.rTensorHom M
130	  invFun := rTensorInv P Q e
131	  left_inv := rTensorInv_leftInverse P Q e
132	  right_inv _ := rTensorInv_injective P Q e (by rw [LinearMap.toFun_eq_coe, rTensorInv_leftInverse])
133	
134	open LinearMap in
135	/-- If there is an `R`-isomorphism between `M ⊗[R] N` and `R`,
136	the induced map `M → Nᵛ` is an isomorphism. -/
137	theorem bijective_curry : Function.Bijective (curry e.toLinearMap) := by
138	  have : curry e.toLinearMap = ((TensorProduct.lid R N).congrLeft _ R ≪≫ₗ e.congrRight) ∘ₗ
139	      rTensorHom N ∘ₗ (ringLmapEquivSelf R R M).symm.toLinearMap := by
140	    rw [← LinearEquiv.toLinearMap_symm_comp_eq]; ext
141	    simp [LinearEquiv.congrLeft, LinearEquiv.congrRight, LinearEquiv.arrowCongrAddEquiv]
142	  simpa [this] using! (rTensorEquiv R M <| TensorProduct.comm R N M ≪≫ₗ e).bijective
143	
144	/-- Given `M ⊗[R] N ≃ₗ[R] R`, this is the induced isomorphism `M ≃ₗ[R] Nᵛ`. -/
145	noncomputable def linearEquivDual : M ≃ₗ[R] Dual R N := .ofBijective _ (bijective_curry e)
146	
147	include e
148	
149	protected theorem right : Module.Invertible R N where
150	  bijective := by
151	    rw [show contractLeft R N = ((linearEquivDual e).rTensor N).symm ≪≫ₗ e by
152	      rw [LinearEquiv.coe_trans, LinearEquiv.eq_comp_toLinearMap_symm]; ext; rfl]
153	    apply LinearEquiv.bijective
154	
155	protected theorem left : Module.Invertible R M := .right (TensorProduct.comm R N M ≪≫ₗ e)
156	
157	instance : Module.Invertible R R := .left (TensorProduct.lid R R)
158	
159	end LinearEquiv
160	
161	variable [Module.Invertible R M]
162	
163	protected theorem congr (e : M ≃ₗ[R] N) : Module.Invertible R N :=
164	  .right (e.symm.lTensor _ ≪≫ₗ linearEquiv R M)
165	
166	variable (R M N)
167	
168	instance : Module.Invertible R (Dual R M) := .left (linearEquiv R M)
169	
170	instance [Module.Invertible R N] : Module.Invertible R (M ⊗[R] N) :=
171	  .right (M := Dual R M ⊗[R] Dual R N) <| tensorTensorTensorComm .. ≪≫ₗ
172	    congr (linearEquiv R M) (linearEquiv R N) ≪≫ₗ TensorProduct.lid R R
173	
174	private theorem finite_projective : Module.Finite R M ∧ Projective R M := by
175	  let N := Dual R M
176	  let e : M ⊗[R] N ≃ₗ[R] R := TensorProduct.comm .. ≪≫ₗ linearEquiv R M
177	  have ⟨S, hS⟩ := TensorProduct.exists_finset (e.symm 1)
178	  let f : (S →₀ N) →ₗ[R] R := Finsupp.lsum R fun i ↦ e.toLinearMap ∘ₗ TensorProduct.mk R M N i.1.1
179	  have : Function.Surjective f := by
180	    rw [← LinearMap.range_eq_top, Ideal.eq_top_iff_one]
181	    use Finsupp.equivFunOnFinite.symm fun i ↦ i.1.2
182	    simp_rw [f, Finsupp.coe_lsum]
183	    rw [Finsupp.sum_fintype _ _ fun _ ↦ map_zero _]
184	    rwa [e.symm_apply_eq, map_sum, ← Finset.sum_coe_sort, eq_comm] at hS
185	  have ⟨g, hg⟩ := projective_lifting_property f .id this
186	  classical
187	  let aux := finsuppRight R _ M N S ≪≫ₗ Finsupp.mapRange.linearEquiv e
188	  let f' : (S →₀ R) →ₗ[R] M := TensorProduct.rid R M ∘ₗ f.lTensor M ∘ₗ aux.symm
189	  let g' : M →ₗ[R] S →₀ R := aux ∘ₗ g.lTensor M ∘ₗ (TensorProduct.rid R M).symm
190	  have : Function.Surjective f' := by simpa [f'] using LinearMap.lTensor_surjective _ this
191	  refine ⟨.of_surjective f' this, .of_split g' f' <| LinearMap.ext fun m ↦ ?_⟩
192	  simp [f', g', show f (g 1) = 1 from DFunLike.congr_fun hg 1]
193	
194	instance : Module.Finite R M := (finite_projective R M).1
195	instance : Projective R M := (finite_projective R M).2
196	example : IsReflexive R M := inferInstance
197	
198	section inj_surj_bij
199	
200	variable {R N P}
201	
202	theorem lTensor_injective_iff {f : N →ₗ[R] P} :
203	    Function.Injective (f.lTensor M) ↔ Function.Injective f := by
204	  refine ⟨fun h ↦ ?_, Flat.lTensor_preserves_injective_linearMap _⟩
205	  rw [← leftCancelEquiv_comp_lTensor_comp_symm (linearEquiv R M) f]
206	  simpa using Flat.lTensor_preserves_injective_linearMap _ h
207	
208	theorem rTensor_injective_iff {f : N →ₗ[R] P} :
209	    Function.Injective (f.rTensor M) ↔ Function.Injective f := by

12	/-!
13	# Faithfully flat modules
14	
15	A module `M` over a commutative ring `R` is *faithfully flat* if it is flat and `IM ≠ M` whenever
16	`I` is a maximal ideal of `R`.
17	
18	## Main declaration
19	
20	- `Module.FaithfullyFlat`: the predicate asserting that an `R`-module `M` is faithfully flat.
21	
22	## Main theorems
23	
24	- `Module.FaithfullyFlat.iff_flat_and_proper_ideal`: an `R`-module `M` is faithfully flat iff it is
25	  flat and for all proper ideals `I` of `R`, `I • M ≠ M`.
26	- `Module.FaithfullyFlat.iff_flat_and_rTensor_faithful`: an `R`-module `M` is faithfully flat iff it
27	  is flat and tensoring with `M` is faithful, i.e. `N ≠ 0` implies `N ⊗ M ≠ 0`.
28	- `Module.FaithfullyFlat.iff_flat_and_lTensor_faithful`: an `R`-module `M` is faithfully flat iff it
29	  is flat and tensoring with `M` is faithful, i.e. `N ≠ 0` implies `M ⊗ N ≠ 0`.
30	- `Module.FaithfullyFlat.iff_exact_iff_rTensor_exact`: an `R`-module `M` is faithfully flat iff
31	  tensoring with `M` preserves and reflects exact sequences, i.e. the sequence `N₁ → N₂ → N₃` is
32	  exact *iff* the sequence `N₁ ⊗ M → N₂ ⊗ M → N₃ ⊗ M` is exact.
33	- `Module.FaithfullyFlat.iff_exact_iff_lTensor_exact`: an `R`-module `M` is faithfully flat iff
34	  tensoring with `M` preserves and reflects exact sequences, i.e. the sequence `N₁ → N₂ → N₃` is
35	  exact *iff* the sequence `M ⊗ N₁ → M ⊗ N₂ → M ⊗ N₃` is exact.
36	- `Module.FaithfullyFlat.iff_zero_iff_lTensor_zero`: an `R`-module `M` is faithfully flat iff for
37	  all linear maps `f : N → N'`, `f = 0` iff `M ⊗ f = 0`.
38	- `Module.FaithfullyFlat.iff_zero_iff_rTensor_zero`: an `R`-module `M` is faithfully flat iff for
39	  all linear maps `f : N → N'`, `f = 0` iff `f ⊗ M = 0`.
40	
41	- `Module.FaithfullyFlat.of_linearEquiv`: modules linearly equivalent to a flat modules are flat
42	- `Module.FaithfullyFlat.trans`: if `S` is `R`-faithfully flat and `M` is `S`-faithfully flat, then
43	  `M` is `R`-faithfully flat.
44	
45	- `Module.FaithfullyFlat.self`: the `R`-module `R` is faithfully flat.
46	
47	-/

64	  submodule_ne_top : ∀ ⦃m : Ideal R⦄ (_ : Ideal.IsMaximal m), m • (⊤ : Submodule R M) ≠ ⊤

66	namespace FaithfullyFlat
67	instance self : FaithfullyFlat R R where
68	  submodule_ne_top m h r := Ideal.eq_top_iff_one _ |>.not.1 h.ne_top <| by
69	    simpa using show 1 ∈ (m • ⊤ : Ideal R) from r.symm ▸ ⟨⟩

73	lemma iff_flat_and_proper_ideal :
74	    FaithfullyFlat R M ↔
75	    (Flat R M ∧ ∀ (I : Ideal R), I ≠ ⊤ → I • (⊤ : Submodule R M) ≠ ⊤) := by
76	  rw [faithfullyFlat_iff]
77	  refine ⟨fun ⟨flat, h⟩ => ⟨flat, fun I hI r => ?_⟩, fun h => ⟨h.1, fun m hm => h.2 _ hm.ne_top⟩⟩
78	  obtain ⟨m, hm, le⟩ := I.exists_le_maximal hI
79	  exact h hm <| eq_top_iff.2 <| show ⊤ ≤ m • ⊤ from r ▸ Submodule.smul_mono le (by simp [r])

82	    FaithfullyFlat R M ↔

240	/-!
241	### Faithfully flat modules and exact sequences
242	
243	In this section we prove that an `R`-module `M` is faithfully flat iff tensoring with `M`
244	preserves and reflects exact sequences.
245	
246	Let `N₁ -l₁₂-> N₂ -l₂₃-> N₃` be two linear maps.
247	- We first show that if `N₁ ⊗ M -> N₂ ⊗ M -> N₃ ⊗ M` is exact, then `N₁ -l₁₂-> N₂ -l₂₃-> N₃` is a
248	  complex, i.e. `range l₁₂ ≤ ker l₂₃`.
249	  This is `range_le_ker_of_exact_rTensor`.
250	- Then in `rTensor_reflects_exact`, we show `ker l₂₃ = range l₁₂` by considering the cohomology
251	  `ker l₂₃ ⧸ range l₁₂`.
252	
253	This shows that when `M` is faithfully flat, `- ⊗ M` reflects exact sequences. For details, see
254	comments in the proof. Since `M` is flat, `- ⊗ M` preserves exact sequences.
255	
256	On the other hand, if `- ⊗ M` preserves and reflects exact sequences, then `M` is faithfully flat.
257	- `M` is flat because `- ⊗ M` preserves exact sequences.
258	- We need to show that if `N ⊗ M = 0` then `N = 0`. Consider the sequence `N -0-> N -0-> 0`. After
259	  tensoring with `M`, we get `N ⊗ M -0-> N ⊗ M -0-> 0` which is exact because `N ⊗ M = 0`.
260	  Since `- ⊗ M` reflects exact sequences, `N = 0`.
261	-/

265	variable {N1 : Type*} [AddCommGroup N1] [Module R N1]
266	variable {N2 : Type*} [AddCommGroup N2] [Module R N2]
267	variable {N3 : Type*} [AddCommGroup N3] [Module R N3]
268	variable (l12 : N1 →ₗ[R] N2) (l23 : N2 →ₗ[R] N3)
269	
270	/--
271	If `M` is faithfully flat, then exactness of `N₁ ⊗ M -> N₂ ⊗ M -> N₃ ⊗ M` implies that the
272	composition `N₁ -> N₂ -> N₃` is `0`.
273	
274	Implementation detail, please use `rTensor_reflects_exact` instead.
275	-/
276	lemma range_le_ker_of_exact_rTensor [fl : FaithfullyFlat R M]
277	    (ex : Function.Exact (l12.rTensor M) (l23.rTensor M)) :
278	    LinearMap.range l12 ≤ LinearMap.ker l23 := by
279	  -- let `n1 ∈ N1`. We need to show `l23 (l12 n1) = 0`. Suppose this is not the case.
280	  rintro _ ⟨n1, rfl⟩
281	  rw [LinearMap.mem_ker]
282	  by_contra! hn1
283	  -- Let `E` be the submodule spanned by `l23 (l12 n1)`. Then because `l23 (l12 n1) ≠ 0`, we have
284	  -- `E ≠ 0`.
285	  let E : Submodule R N3 := Submodule.span R {l23 (l12 n1)}
286	  have hE : Nontrivial E :=
287	    ⟨0, ⟨⟨l23 (l12 n1), Submodule.mem_span_singleton_self _⟩, Subtype.coe_ne_coe.1 hn1.symm⟩⟩
288	  -- Since `N1 ⊗ M -> N2 ⊗ M -> N3 ⊗ M` is exact, we have `l23 (l12 n1) ⊗ₜ m = 0` for all `m : M`.
289	  have eq1 : ∀ (m : M), l23 (l12 n1) ⊗ₜ[R] m = 0 := fun m ↦
290	    ex.apply_apply_eq_zero (n1 ⊗ₜ[R] m)
291	  -- Then `E ⊗ M = 0`. Indeed,
292	  have eq0 : (⊤ : Submodule R (E ⊗[R] M)) = ⊥ := by
293	    -- suppose `x ∈ E ⊗ M`. We will show `x = 0`.
294	    ext x
295	    simp only [Submodule.mem_top, Submodule.mem_bot, true_iff]
296	    have mem : x ∈ (⊤ : Submodule R _) := ⟨⟩
297	    rw [← TensorProduct.span_tmul_eq_top, Submodule.mem_span_set] at mem
298	    obtain ⟨c, hc, rfl⟩ := mem
299	    choose b a hy using hc
300	    let r : ⦃a : E ⊗[R] M⦄ → a ∈ ↑c.support → R := fun a ha =>
301	      Submodule.mem_span_singleton.1 (b ha).2 |>.choose
302	    have hr : ∀ ⦃i : E ⊗[R] M⦄ (hi : i ∈ c.support), b hi =
303	        r hi • ⟨l23 (l12 n1), Submodule.mem_span_singleton_self _⟩ := fun a ha =>
304	      Subtype.ext <| Submodule.mem_span_singleton.1 (b ha).2 |>.choose_spec.symm
305	    -- Since `M` is flat and `E -> N1` is injective, we only need to check that x = 0
306	    -- in `N1 ⊗ M`. We write `x = ∑ μᵢ • (l23 (l12 n1)) ⊗ mᵢ = ∑ μᵢ • 0 = 0`
307	    -- (remember `E = span {l23 (l12 n1)}` and `eq1`)
308	    refine Finset.sum_eq_zero fun i hi => show c i • i = 0 from
309	      (Module.Flat.rTensor_preserves_injective_linearMap (M := M) E.subtype <|
310	              Submodule.injective_subtype E) ?_
311	    rw [← hy hi, hr hi, smul_tmul, map_smul, LinearMap.rTensor_tmul, Submodule.subtype_apply, eq1,
312	      smul_zero, map_zero]
313	  have : Subsingleton (E ⊗[R] M) := subsingleton_iff_forall_eq 0 |>.2 fun x =>
314	    show x ∈ (⊥ : Submodule R _) from eq0 ▸ ⟨⟩
315	  -- but `E ⊗ M = 0` implies `E = 0` because `M` is faithfully flat and this is a contradiction.
316	  exact not_subsingleton_iff_nontrivial.2 inferInstance <| fl.rTensor_reflects_triviality R M E
317	
318	lemma rTensor_reflects_exact [fl : FaithfullyFlat R M]
319	    (ex : Function.Exact (l12.rTensor M) (l23.rTensor M)) :
320	    Function.Exact l12 l23 := LinearMap.exact_iff.2 <| by

18	# Flat modules
19	
20	A module `M` over a commutative semiring `R` is *mono-flat* if for all monomorphisms of modules
21	(i.e., injective linear maps) `N →ₗ[R] P`, the canonical map `N ⊗ M → P ⊗ M` is injective
22	(cf. [Katsov2004], [KatsovNam2011]).
23	To show a module is mono-flat, it suffices to check inclusions of finitely generated
24	submodules `N` into finitely generated modules `P`, and `P` can be further assumed to lie in
25	the same universe as `R`.
26	
27	`M` is flat if `· ⊗ M` preserves finite limits (equivalently, pullbacks, or equalizers).
28	If `R` is a ring, an `R`-module `M` is flat if and only if it is mono-flat, and to show
29	a module is flat, it suffices to check inclusions of finitely generated ideals into `R`.
30	See <https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/00HD>.
31	
32	Currently, `Module.Flat` is defined to be equivalent to mono-flatness over a semiring.
33	It is left as a TODO item to introduce the genuine flatness over semirings and rename
34	the current `Module.Flat` to `Module.MonoFlat`.
35	
36	## Main declaration
37	
38	* `Module.Flat`: the predicate asserting that an `R`-module `M` is flat.
39	
40	## Main theorems
41	
42	* `Module.Flat.of_retract`: retracts of flat modules are flat
43	* `Module.Flat.of_linearEquiv`: modules linearly equivalent to a flat module are flat
44	* `Module.Flat.directSum`: arbitrary direct sums of flat modules are flat
45	* `Module.Flat.of_free`: free modules are flat
46	* `Module.Flat.of_projective`: projective modules are flat
47	* `Module.Flat.preserves_injective_linearMap`: If `M` is a flat module then tensoring with `M`
48	  preserves injectivity of linear maps. This lemma is fully universally polymorphic in all
49	  arguments, i.e. `R`, `M` and linear maps `N → N'` can all have different universe levels.
50	* `Module.Flat.iff_rTensor_preserves_injective_linearMap`: a module is flat iff tensoring modules
51	  in the higher universe preserves injectivity.
52	* `Module.Flat.lTensor_exact`: If `M` is a flat module then tensoring with `M` is an exact
53	  functor. This lemma is fully universally polymorphic in all arguments, i.e.
54	  `R`, `M` and linear maps `N → N' → N''` can all have different universe levels.
